reviews.title: Reading tracker
reviews.text: Honestly this is probably the least user friendly reading tracker I’ve ever used. I only have it because my library does events through it.

reviews.title: Needs a lot of work
reviews.text: With a toddler we read multiple books at a time it would be nice to add more than one book or tell how many times we read it instead of having to enter it 3 different times

reviews.title: Time consuming
reviews.text: I think this app would be great for older kids reading longer books but when your trying to read 1,000 books before kindergarten it takes a while to log books. First you have to select your child, click on where you add a book, scan the book, click on the book that pops up and then click the you did it page. If you are just adding a couple books it’s not bad but if you sit down and read 8-10 book doing all those steps over and over take a while. Especially when your kiddo just sat through multiple books and is now up running around getting into things. It just seems like there would be a more efficient way. Maybe to scan multiple books and select and add them all in a group.

reviews.title: Scrolling big
reviews.text: There’s an issue where I am scrolling through my log of completed titles and it just goes into an epileptic fit after a couple pages. If I want to see what books I read a year ago, I flat out can’t because it just freaks out.

reviews.title: Used to be great
reviews.text: I like that you can use an in app timer to record your points and scanner to scan the barcode of your books but they stopped giving away actual prizes for adults and I don’t feel the app is worth it anymore. They give you stickers but what adult wants to drive all the way down to the library for a sticker? Nobody. I really wish they would bring prizes back with the raffle. It was a lot of fun and made me want read more.

reviews.title: So Laborious
reviews.text:
The user interface on this app is terrible. To log a book I have to click:

+ > reading > select reader > choose reader > select title (titles hardly ever come up via the search feature so I usually use isbn, so I have to scan the book) > uncheck “track progress” > save > and then I can choose quick complete BUT if I’m logging reading from the night before then I have to go on to > log reading > tap calendar > change date > save > check “book finished” > done

This is insane!

I have two kids and we read a lot. Sometimes together, sometimes separately. Logging a single book should not be this cumbersome. There should be a way to log within a users profile without having to “select user” every time, to multi add several books all at once, and to add one book to multiple users at once.

Update 7/20: I can’t believe it they added ANOTHER THING TO CLICK. Now when I log a book it “congratulates” me and I have to click “done.” At this point I’m encouraged to read to my kids even more so we can hit the 1000 books before kindergarten faster and I can be done with this horrible app.

reviews.title: Crashes constantly
reviews.text: I haven't been able to use the app as it crashes the second I try to open it. I do have a new iPhone 17, and for some reason, the app just doesn't perform well on this phone, whereas before I never had issues opening it on my iPhone 13 mini. For that reason, I’ve been using the website version on my phone, but I think it could still be improved to enhance usability. For example, I have to click two different buttons to start the timer when it could be the initial “start timer” button. Also, I remember being able to scan the book, but I can't easily find this option anymore. Maybe that option isn't there anymore?

reviews.title: Buggy and not intuitive
reviews.text:
The app was already tedious to use, but I decided to use it as a method of tracking how much time I spendreading for a reading challenge I'm on this year. After the latest update, all my historical reading stats are gone. Even reading I logged after the update doesn't appear. Thankfully my stats still appear from the desktop app, but this is a pretty big error. 

Other than this latest issue, the app just isn't great to use. Books frequently don't appear when I try to search them for the first time to track my reading. Additionally, when manually logging reading time, the app forces you to log in minutes. Having to do math just to log my reading is annoying. The desktop site is again better here, allowing you to log in a simple hours and minutes format (for example, the website lets you enter "2 hr 15 min," while the app makes you enter "135" mins).

reviews.title: Does not work for big readers.
reviews.text:
App works well enough and is user friendly. However, my son reads for hours at a time. It will not allow you to log more than 180 minutes for a single session, and you must click an additional button promising that you are being truthful about the minutes logged if you do log the maximum allowed. 
In addition to that, there is a maximum number of minutes you are allowed to log in a single day. My son read for six hours yesterday as it was an early-release day for school. He cannot get credit for it due to app limitations. 
Developers:
Some kids really love reading. Some kids just really love the rewards they get from reading long hours. Either way, please consider removing limitations so I can accurately and truthfully document my son’s reading sessions.
